title: Near Simultaneous Laser Scanning Confocal and Atomic Force Microscopy (Conpokal) on Live Cells
protocol: Turn on the power sources for both the confocal microscope and the atomic force microscope.
Allow instruments to thermally equilibrate and stabilize, typically for 1 hour.
Prepare a clean, system-approved glass-bottomed Petri dish.
Fill the preparation dish half full with phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Create data storage folders for the confocal and AFM on the computer's hard drive.
Inoculate Streptococcus mutans bacteria using an inoculation loop in 15 mL of Todd Hewitt Yeast (THY) overnight in a 5% CO2 incubator for exponential phase.
Coat experimental sample dishes with 1 mL of poly-l-lysine solution and leave them in the biosafety cabinet for 1 h.
Aspirate the poly-l-lysine solution after setting and rinse the dishes 3 times with PBS.
Inoculate THY with 1 mL of bacterial suspension until an optical density of 0.6 – 0.7 is achieved.
Add 1 mL of new bacteria solution to each poly-l-lysine-coated dish and incubate for 1 h.
During the last 10 min, add 1 mL of green fluorescent membrane stain (concentration of 1 µM) to each dish.
Rinse each dish 3 times with PBS after adding the stain.
Fix bacteria gently with about 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde solution for 15 min at room temperature inside a biosafety cabinet.
Rinse each dish 3 times with PBS after fixation.
Store Human Embryonic Kidney (HEK) 293 cells in liquid nitrogen.
Perform fast thawing of HEK 293 cells at 37°C water bath before plating.
Add 1 mL of basement membrane matrix solution in cell culture media to each cell sample dish.
Incubate the dishes (5% CO2) at 37 °C for 1 h.
Aspirate the solution and wash the dishes with cell culture media.
Plate the required number of HEK 293 cells (e.g., 100,000 cells per 35 mm dish).
Add 2 mL of cell culture media to each dish.
Incubate the cells (5% CO2) at 37 °C for 48 h.
After 48 h, add 2 µL of a fluorescent microtubule cytoskeleton dye (concentration of 1x) to each cell sample dish.
Incubate the dishes for 30 min.
Aspirate the solution containing the dye and wash the cells 3 times with PBS.
Add 2 mL of cell culture media to each dish.
Add 1 µL of plasma membrane dye (concentration of 10 µM) to the sample dishes.
Incubate the dishes for 30 minutes.
Wash the solution containing the dye 3 times with PBS and add 2 mL of cell culture media.
Counterstain the nucleus by adding 1 µL of a nucleic acid dye (concentration of 10 µM) solution to the sample dishes.
Incubate the dishes for 30 min.
Wash the solution containing the dye 3 times with PBS and add 2 mL of culture media.
Load the clean, system-approved Petri dish half full of PBS.
If sample stage has built-in clasps, use these.
Otherwise, use vacuum grease to stabilize the sample.
Mount the AFM chip into the glass block using gloves, tweezers, and a small screwdriver.
Place the AFM chip onto the glass block and center it.
Ensure that the cantilever is in the visible, non-opaque portion of the mounting block.
Secure the chip with the screwdriver by tightening until snug against the glass block.
Check the orientation of the AFM cantilever using a stereo microscope or handheld spyglass.
Adjust the cantilever orientation as needed.
Place the glass block into the AFM head in the proper orientation and lock it in place.
Locate the bottom of the calibration dish using the brightfield option of the confocal microscope.
Note the z height where the bottom of the dish is located with respect to the microscope objective.
Move the AFM cantilever upwards 2000 µm using the motor control panel on the computer that operates the z stepper motors.
Gently place the AFM head with the AFM chip onto the sample stage, ensuring each vertical point on the AFM head is firmly set in its designated groove on the AFM stage.
Visually check how close the cantilever holder is to the dish.
If the cantilever holder appears too close to the top of the sample dish, back it out using the z stepper motors before lowering the AFM tip towards the sample.
Using brightfield illumination, slowly lower the AFM chip to the bottom of the glass dish using the z stepper motor control panel on the AFM software.
Locate the manual micrometers that control x-y or in-plane motion of the AFM head on the instrument platform.
Adjust the position of the AFM cantilever within the field of view by correcting the AFM head as the cantilever comes into view.
Lower the AFM tip with steps of 100 – 200 µm to avoid crashing the AFM tip into the Petri dish.
Watch for a shadow to appear on the microscope software view, which indicates the AFM tip is getting closer to the bottom of the dish.
Decrease increments to 20 – 50 µm as the tip approaches the bottom.
Adjust the look up tables (LUTs) of the camera image as the tip lowers into the dish by using the LUTs panel on the confocal software.
Continue to lower the AFM tip using small steps until it is mostly in-focus.
Ensure that the tip is dark enough so that the general shape of it can be seen and centered in the field of view.
Confirm that the tip appears blurry, which indicates it has not encountered the bottom of the dish.
Adjust the microscope focus to ensure the tip is in focus.
Use the microscope measurement tool to collect the width and length of the AFM cantilever.
Remove the laser light filter if present.
Ensure the AFM laser is on and visible through the optics.
Move the laser into the field of view near the AFM tip using the alignment dials.
Replace the laser light filter after positioning the laser.
Place the laser on the backside of where the AFM tip is located on the cantilever.
Adjust the mirror manually until a sum signal greater than 0.0 V is obtained.
Move the laser in small amounts to achieve the maximum sum signal at the AFM tip position.
Once the laser position is set, zero the vertical and lateral deflection using the manually controlled dials.
Observe the laser alignment panel on the AFM software.
Use vertical and lateral deflection knobs to center the red dot in the crosshairs.
Turn off the confocal microscope light source.
Close the AFM enclosure if applicable.
Input all experiment specific information in the calibration window.
Press the calibration button to allow automatic system calibration.
Note the stiffness of the cantilever (N/m) and its sensitivity (nm/V).
Retract the AFM cantilever at least 2000 µm with stepper motors.
Take the AFM head off the stage.
Remove the calibration dish.
Rotate or insert the desired objective.
Retract the objective 10% of the working distance if programmed to do so.
Place one drop of immersion oil on the eye of the objective for an oil objective.
Use a cotton swab to apply small dabs of vacuum grease around the edge of the sample ring within the sample stage.
Load the sample dish carefully into the sample stage.
Rotate the sample a few times to ensure a good seal with the grease.
Raise the objective to the bottom of the dish until oil wicks over the eye of the objective.
Focus the imaging system on the sample without the AFM head on the stage.
Note the z height for reference.
Carefully replace the AFM head onto the platform.
Lower the tip towards the sample using the z stepper motors.
Adjust look up tables (LUTs) in the brightfield image as needed.
Move the AFM head manually so that the tip is centered or left-centered in the field of view.
Readjust the laser position using the manual micrometers on the AFM head.
Zero the vertical deflections by adjusting the respective knobs.
Recalibrate the AFM cantilever in the sample dish.
Recalibrate the AFM cantilever inside of the calibration dish if using contact mode and a different medium than the sample.
Replace the current attenuating light filter with the one that blocks all AFM laser light for confocal microscope images.
Lower the tip to the bottom of the sample dish using the automated approach command button.
Set the size/area of the scan on the imaging control panel.
Set the resolution on the imaging control panel.
Set the setpoint on the imaging control panel.
Set the z length on the imaging control panel.
Set the pixel time (or use calibrated/propagated values) on the imaging control panel.
Begin scanning.
Lift the AFM chip 50 – 100 µm up after completing a scan.
Navigate to a new measurement position in the sample dish.
Approach the glass and start to scan again.
Select the Autosave option or manually save each generated file by clicking Save.
Open the confocal operating software.
Ensure all associated peripherals, light sources, and controllers are switched on and functioning normally.
Rotate or insert an objective of low magnification (10x or 20x) to view the sample.
Ensure the objective is at a safe working distance from where the sample dish will be placed.
Back-out the objective if needed to avoid potential collision with the sample.
Dab vacuum grease around the edge of the sample dish ring using a cotton swab.
Place a single drop of immersion oil onto the front lens of the objective if using an oil objective.
Place the desired sample into the sample stage.
Spin the sample around to ensure that vacuum grease has generated a tight bond to the sample stage insert or employ sample clips.
If using an oil objective, raise the objective to the bottom of the dish so the oil just wicks over the glass bottom.
Minimize ambient lighting to avoid excessive bleaching.
Locate the sample using brightfield or epifluorescence modes via the camera or eyepieces.
Using the focus knob, focus on an area of interest containing multiple cells or a single cell.
Adjust the AFM position within the confocal field of view by using the motor control panel in the AFM software to align with the features being imaged.
Capture images in bright-field or epifluorescence based on the sample label and microscope software settings.
Using microscope software, select confocal capabilities panel.
Choose laser lines appropriate for sample dyes.
Turn on lasers to excite and image sample features.
Set gain to 70 to optimize fluorescence and limit noise.
Adjust laser power between 1 – 3 % to avoid saturation.
Set pinhole size to 1 Airy unit for resolution maximization.
Increase pinhole size if sample is dim with high laser power.
Start with a pixel dwell time of 2 µs, adjust as needed.
Let instrument calculate optimal pixel size via Nyquist option.
Select Scan option on software and begin data collection.
Use the shortest wavelength for calculation of spacing when multiple laser lines are used.
Save the file to the appropriate folder after acquisition finishes.
Define the volume by selecting the middle plane if prior knowledge of the sample’s thickness exists.
Set the top to half the sample thickness above the middle plane.
Set the bottom to half the thickness below the middle plane.
Find another place of interest on the sample and repeat image collection steps after completing data collection in one field of view or when the sample bleaches.
Retract the AFM chip using z stepper motors at least 2000 µm or the distance traveled to reach the sample surface.
Remove the AFM head from the stage carefully and place it in its resting position.
Retract the microscope objective far away from the sample.
Remove the sample and clean off any grease or oil from the bottom of the sample dish.
Acquire a new, clean Petri dish and fill it with 70% ethanol solution one-half to three-quarters full.
Place the Petri dish into the sample holder and replace the AFM head to allow the AFM chip to soak in the ethanol for 5 minutes.
Begin copying experiment data onto an external hard drive while the AFM chip soaks.
Remove the AFM head after soaking the AFM chip in ethanol for at least 5 minutes.
Place the AFM chip holder into the mounting station using gloves.
Carefully remove the AFM chip from its holder using tweezers with rubber grips.
Return the used tip back to its box oriented off axis to indicate it has been used.
Take the Petri dish filled with ethanol solution out of the system.
Dispose of the liquid and the dish.
Gently clean the oil from the microscope objective using gloves, lens cleaner, and lens wipes following standard protocols.
Clean the sample holder by removing any grease.
Dispose of all waste materials according to biosafety protocols.
Return tools to their known locations.
Finish data collection from the computer(s).
Shut down the computers.
Power off all instruments, accessories, peripherals, or other devices utilized for the experiment.
